question: Is there a worthwhile active-rectifier opportunity? Choose one concrete circuit and exact devices, get their applicable hot Rds(on), quantify the added losses, and compare across the bridge bracket.
focus: 1) Choose ONE specific active-rectifier circuit for a 400 V bus / 120 V / 15 A true-RMS PFC input: name the topology and a specific controller. 2) Choose up to three exact MOSFET candidates: real order code, package, pinout (note any Kelvin/source-sense pin), and blocking voltage headroom for a 400 V bus. 3) Obtain each candidate's applicable HOT Rds(on) at the real operating junction temperature and gate bias from PRIMARY manufacturer sources - not a 25 C maximum, not a headline figure. Record document revision, page and condition. 4) Quantify P_additional as far as sources allow: gate-drive and rail generation, controller supply, current sensing, dead time and a safe fail-off state, and the conducted/radiated EMI re-assessment obligation. Where a term cannot be sourced, report it as an explicit unknown rather than zero. 5) Compute P_saved = 450*R_hot ... i.e. P_saved = P_bridge - 450*R_hot - P_additional across the bridge bracket 23-35 W, and state whether any candidate beats the 51-78 mOhm pre-additional break-even. 6) State the single missing input most likely to change the conclusion.
stop_rule: No substitute device, no undocumented digitization, no hot-Rds extrapolation from a 25 C maximum, and no zero-filling P_additional. A conclusion of 'no opportunity at the break-even' is a valid and useful result. If no concrete circuit can be sourced, return UNKNOWN with the capture failures.
